My current finding is that the “\(n\)-tastic’’ condition forces the side‑length ratios to approach the golden‑ratio limit: as \(n\to\infty\),

\[
\frac{BD}{CD}= \frac{F_n}{F_{n+1}}\longrightarrow\frac1\varphi,\qquad 
\frac{BC}{BD}=1+\frac{CD}{BD}\longrightarrow\varphi^2,
\]

so the triangle’s shape becomes independent of the absolute size (the semiperimeter \(s\) can be taken arbitrarily large, giving \(AB\approx AC\) and incircle radius \(r\to\frac{BC}{2}\)). Consequently the ratio \(\displaystyle\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) has a well‑defined limit \(\alpha\) that depends only on the limiting angle at \(A\), i.e. only on the golden‑ratio \(\varphi\). This reduces the problem to computing \(\alpha\) for the “asymptotic’’ triangle with \(BD:CD=1:\varphi\).

My current finding is that the maximal value \(a_{2n}= \frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) for the even‑indexed “\(2n\)-tastic’’ triangles converges to the constant  

\[
\alpha=\lim_{n\to\infty}a_{2n}=2+\sqrt5 .
\]

Numerically, for \(n=2,4,6,8\) the values are \(3,\;4,\;4.2,\;55/13\approx4.2308\), which approach \(2+\sqrt5\approx4.23607\). The limit equals \(\varphi^{3}\) where \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\), and \(\varphi^{3}=2+\sqrt5\). Hence \(p=2,\;q=5\) and  

\[
\big\lfloor p^{\,q^{p}}\big\rfloor = 2^{5^{2}} = 2^{25}=33\,554\,432,
\qquad 33\,554\,432\bmod 99\,991 = 57\,447 .
\]

My current finding is a closed‑form expression for the maximal ratio  

\[
a_n=\max\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

over all \(n\)-tastic triangles.  
Using the incircle tangency lengths \(BD=F_n,\;CD=F_{n+1}\) we obtain the side lengths  

\[
BC=F_{n+2},\qquad AB=s-F_{n+1},\qquad AC=s-F_n,
\]

with any semiperimeter \(s>F_{n+2}\).  
Imposing the cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) forces a unique value of \(s\) given by  

\[
s=\frac{F_{n+2}F_{n+1}}{F_{n+1}-F_n}= \frac{F_{n+2}F_{n+1}}{F_{n-1}} .
\]

With this \(s\) the ratio simplifies to  

\[
{a_n=\frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}}}.
\]

Thus for even indices \(2n\),

\[
a_{2n}= \frac{F_{2n+2}}{F_{2n-1}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\phi^{3}=2+\sqrt5,
\]

so \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\). This yields the final answer after the required modular exponentiation.

My current finding is that for an \(n\)-tastic triangle the ratio  

\[
\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}=a_n
\]

is uniquely determined by the parameter \(t=s-a>0\) (the excess of the semiperimeter over \(BC\)). Solving the cyclic condition \(K,N,K',B\) ∈ a circle gives a single root \(t_n\) for each \(n\ge2\). Numerically  

\[
a_2=3,\;a_4\approx4.0000,\;a_6\approx4.2000,\;a_8\approx4.23077,\;a_{10}\approx4.23529,\dots
\]

and the even‑indexed values converge rapidly to  

\[
\alpha=\lim_{n\to\infty}a_{2n}=2+\sqrt5\approx4.23607.
\]

Thus \(p=2,\;q=5\) and  

\[
\big\lfloor p^{\,q^{\,p}}\big\rfloor=\big\lfloor2^{5^2}\big\rfloor=2^{25}=33\,554\,432\equiv57447\pmod{99991}.
\]

My current finding is that for every \(n\ge2\) the cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) forces a unique “large‑\(s\)” solution with semiperimeter \(s\) satisfying  
\[
s=\frac{F_{n+2}F_{n+1}}{F_{n+1}-F_n}= \frac{F_{n+2}F_{n+1}}{F_{n-1}} .
\]  
For this solution the ratio simplifies to a closed form  
\[
a_n=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}= \frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}} .
\]  
Consequently for even indices \(a_{2n}=F_{2n+2}/F_{2n-1}\to\phi^3=2+\sqrt5\), giving \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\) and the final answer \({57447}\). This rules out the “small‑\(s\)” roots (which make the ratio unbounded) as invalid for the problem.

My current finding is a closed‑form formula for the maximal ratio: for every \(n\ge2\) one has  

\[
a_n=\max\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}= \frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}},
\]

where \(F_k\) are the Fibonacci numbers \((F_0=0,F_1=1)\). Consequently for even indices  

\[
a_{2m}= \frac{F_{2m+2}}{F_{2m-1}}\xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{}\varphi^{3}=2+\sqrt5,
\]

so \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\). This matches the numerical values \(a_2=3,\;a_4=4,\;a_6=4.2,\dots\) and gives the final answer \(\lfloor2^{5^{2}}\rfloor\bmod 99991=57447\).

My current finding is a closed‑form expression for the maximal ratio: for every \(n\ge2\),

\[
a_n=\max\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}= \frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}},
\]

where \(F_k\) are the Fibonacci numbers (\(F_0=0,F_1=1\)).  
Consequently for even indices \(a_{2m}=F_{2m+2}/F_{2m-1}\to\varphi^{3}=2+\sqrt5\).  
This gives \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\) and the required remainder \(\displaystyle\big\lfloor2^{5^{2}}\big\rfloor\bmod 99991=57447\).  
The formula matches all numerical tests (e.g. \(a_2=3,\;a_4=4,\;a_6=4.2,\;a_8=4.230769\ldots\)).

My current finding is that for an \(n\)-tastic triangle the ratio  
\[
R_n=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]
has a unique value (the cyclic condition \(K,N,K',B\) determines a single incircle radius \(r\) for each \(n\)). Computing \(R_n\) for even \(n\) gives  

\[
R_2=3,\;R_4=4,\;R_6=4.2,\;R_8=\frac{55}{13}\approx4.23077,\;R_{10}\approx4.23529,\;R_{12}\approx4.23596,
\]

and the sequence converges rapidly to \(2+\sqrt5\). Hence \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\) (so \(p=2,q=5\)). Consequently  
\[
\big\lfloor p^{\,q^{\,p}}\big\rfloor=2^{5^2}=2^{25}=33\,554\,432,
\]
and \(33\,554\,432\bmod 99\,991=57\,447\). This matches all numeric checks up to \(n=12\) and shows the limit is indeed \(2+\sqrt5\).

My current finding is a closed‑form expression for the maximal ratio: for every \(n\ge2\) the unique “large‑\(s\)” triangle that satisfies the cyclic condition yields  

\[
a_n=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}= \frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}},
\]

where \(F_k\) are the Fibonacci numbers (\(F_0=0,F_1=1\)). Consequently for even indices  

\[
a_{2m}= \frac{F_{2m+2}}{F_{2m-1}}\xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{}\varphi^{3}=2+\sqrt5,
\]

so \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\). This gives \(\lfloor2^{5^{2}}\rfloor=2^{25}=33\,554\,432\) and  

\[
33\,554\,432\bmod 99991 = 57447.
\]

My current finding is that the cyclic condition \(KNK'B\) forces the incircle radius \(r\) (with \(BD=F_n,\,CD=F_{n+1}\) and \(BC=F_{n+2}\)) to satisfy one of three equations, giving three admissible radii:
\[
r\approx0.2008114,\;0.4858683,\;0.6180339.
\]
Evaluating the required ratio
\[
R=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]
for each radius yields
\[
R_1=2+\sqrt5\approx4.23607,\qquad
R_2=\frac{\sqrt{6+\sqrt5}}2\approx1.43493,\qquad
R_3=\frac{\sqrt2}2\approx0.70711.
\]
Since \(a_n\) is the maximum possible value of \(R\) for an \(n\)-tastic triangle, we have \(a_{2n}=2+\sqrt5\) for all large \(n\). Hence \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\) (so \(p=2,\;q=5\)). Consequently
\[
\big\lfloor p^{\,q^{\,p}}\big\rfloor=2^{5^2}=2^{25}=33\,554\,432,
\]
and \(33\,554\,432\bmod 99991=57447\). This shows the answer is \({57447}\).
